one_month_reasoning: No Cipher earnings in the window. EDGAR shows no Q3-date 8-K and Q3-25 was reported Nov 3, so the print most likely lands just after Oct 31 (round 1 wrongly called 11/02 'scheduled'). In-window drivers: (1) late-October Amazon/Microsoft/Alphabet/Meta Q3 prints and 2027 capex commentary, the main sector driver; I lean mildly positive on capex but the group has negative momentum after a ~30% slide. (2) The Oct-28 FOMC with the 10-yr at 5.24%; long-duration, levered names are rate-sensitive. (3) Barber Lake's first hall rent is due 'in Q4-26' (8-K), a possible small positive release. (4) Lease news at Reveille/Ulysses/Odessa is possible but unscheduled; I dropped the unsourced 'Morgan Stanley expected deals by October' claim. (5) ERCOT audit RFIs are ongoing; the report is due Dec 10, outside the window. The V3/Bitfury tranches settle a forward hedged in Nov-2025, so they are not new supply. Net: a near-symmetric lognormal, median ~$15.3 (slight drift down from momentum and my below-spot fair value), sigma ~0.30 (112%/3.5 = 32%). Round 4: unchanged. The split-rate DCF and site fixes are valuation changes with no catalyst in the window, and a 1-month forecast should not lean on them.

fair_value.method: 60% split-rate DCF ($7.05 = contracted $4.47 with AWS terms at 6.75%, Fluidstack 7.75%, AI-lab 8.0%, residual and pipeline at 8.5%, plus $2.57 site-by-site pipeline) and 40% EV/EBITDA ($10.61 = 15x 2028 EBITDA $583M less $4.78B net debt plus $1.27B pipeline). Blend $8.47, rounded $8.5. On a single 8.5% rate the DCF is $6.14 and the blend $7.93.

bear.story: The AI-infrastructure de-rating continues and the market pays only for the contracted book (~$4.5/sh 12m-forward after re-lease and refit costs) plus a token pipeline. Triggers: hall slips at Barber Lake/Stingray, overruns past the $359M layer, the ERCOT audit stalling Batch Zero, a discounted parent raise, or doubts over Fluidstack funding its refresh and the unnamed AI lab's credit.

base.story: Barber Lake reaches full rent by Q1-27 and Stingray starts Apr/May-27; run-rate NOI ~$700M. One of Reveille/Ulysses signs at peer-like rents. The stock trades above my fair value because the sector pays for pipeline optionality more generously than my probability-weighted values.

bull.story: 500 MW-1 GW of new hyperscaler/AI-lab leases (Reveille, Ulysses, Odessa, an early Batch-Zero site) at TeraWulf/Applied Digital-like economics, ERCOT confirming multi-GW, and the market valuing signed AWS-type leases near their ~6-6.5% secured cost. Above $16.03 the 2031 converts dilute.

thesis_break_reason: Contracted-only value is $4.47/share 12m-forward (~$4.0 today) at the split rates, after re-lease cuts, refit capex and the AI-lab haircut, on 494M FD shares and $4.88B net debt. $6.0 is that plus ~$0.75B of pipeline (Reveille/Ulysses/Odessa near-term at ~2/3 of my probability-weighted value). Below it the market is impairing signed leases (AWS delay/termination, Fluidstack stress beyond the Google backstop, the AI-lab commitment failing to convert, overruns well past $359M) or pricing a deeply discounted raise, not just removing the pipeline. Lowered from $7.5 because contracted value fell ~$1.5/sh on the round-3 supervisor's terminal corrections and site-level NOI.

reasoning: Round 4 rebuilds the DCF site by site from the checked inventory and splits the discount rate. (1) Sites: the stale Q2-26 company NOI schedule is replaced by each lease's own terms and hall dates (Black Pearl $296M yr-1, 216 IT MW; Stingray $107.5M, 70 IT MW; Barber Lake $331.5M, 207 IT MW, Fluidstack to ~2037 then the AI lab to ~2047). 2028 NOI is $705M, 3% below the company's $727M. Every inventory site now appears once: Odessa mining is added (~$45M) in the same row as its 25% HPC conversion; Ulysses and Reveille are valued only in the near-term bucket (double count removed); Colchis at 76%; Milsing and both expansions get explicit MW and probabilities; the Canaan shares (~$18M) go into net debt. Pipeline falls from $1.50B to $1.125B ($3.43 to $2.57/sh). (2) Round-3 supervisor corrections: a re-lease rent cut (85%) and refit capex ($2M/IT MW) at every expiry, the same mechanics at the Barber Lake 2047 expiry, and a 12.5% expected loss on the unbacked AI-lab rent. Together with the site-level NOI these cut single-rate EV from $7.50B to $6.44B. (3) Split rates: AWS-term rent at 6.75% (secured notes at 6.0-6.125% plus ~65bp for the unfinanced residual, the term beyond 2031 and completion risk), Fluidstack term 7.75% (its notes cost 7.125%), AI-lab 8.0%, and everything after the contracts at 8.5%. That adds $0.40B of EV (+$0.91/sh). DCF: single $6.14, split $7.05 (round 3 $9.38 single). EV/EBITDA $12.09 to $10.61. Fair value $10.5 to $8.5. Ladder: median from ~$13.6 to ~$12.9 (about a third of the log-distance from spot to the new fair value, a bit less than round 3's ~40%, since most of the fair value cut comes from conservative long-dated terminal assumptions that the market rarely prices over 12 months); sigma ~0.80; right tail trimmed slightly for 2031-convert dilution. Thesis break $7.5 to $6.0. The 1-month ladder is unchanged. Research: no web searches; the inventory supplied primary-source facts, Twelve Data gave the Canaan and BTC prices, and the GPU-life fact-check corrected IREN (5 yrs, not 6) and Nebius (5); base life stays 6 (CoreWeave 6, hyperscalers 5-6).
